Theme

Latin word

cūrō

cūrō, cūrāre, cūrāvī, cūrātum

verb, first conjugation

care about; look after, take care of; see to it (that), take care (that); see to, take charge of; arrange for (something to be done)

In this lexicon

  • care

    the recommended word · classical · Plaut. Most. 627: nōn ego istuc cūrō quī sit quid sit unde sit; Cic. N. D. 2.167: magna dī cūrant, parva neglegunt; Traupman 94: Ista nōn cūrō.; Traupman 103: I don’t mind that …, nōn cūrō quod (+ indic.)

  • care

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Att. 2.2.1: cūrā, amābō tē, Cicerōnem nostrum; Cato, Agr. 54: bovēs bene cūrāre

  • ensure

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fam. 7.20.3: cūrā ut valeās; Plaut. Am. 1.2.25; Cic. Div. 1.48 (Lewis & Short)

  • manage

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 4.13.7 (Lewis & Short): cūrāre omnia studiōsissimē ac dīligentissimē; Traupman 343

  • organise

    also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.13 (Lewis & Short): pontem in Ararī faciundum

Examples

  • Nōn ego istuc cūrō quī sit quid sit unde sit

    I don’t care who he is, what he is or where he comes from.Plaut. Most. 627
